title: MCV–RDW tensor interactions do not improve frozen HbA1c prediction beyond separate red-cell indices in two NHANES cohorts
abstract: We tested whether joint mean corpuscular volume (MCV) and red-cell distribution width (RDW) structure improves concurrent HbA1c prediction beyond fasting glucose and flexible separate red-cell indices. Additive spline ridge models were trained in NHANES2011–2012 (n=2280) and evaluated frozen in separately recruited2013–2014 participants (n=2360). Adding25 centered MCV×RDW spline products changed fasting-subsample-weighted MSE from 0.24524212 to 0.25205647 percentage-points squared, delta +0.00681434 (joint source/target PSU-bootstrap95% interval [+0.00007457,+0.03592360]). The registered improvement criterion failed. This exploratory reused-data result concerns one interaction representation and concurrent prediction, not red-cell lifespan, true glycemic discordance or clinical diagnosis. Independent-program validation remains unperformed.
